pages.text: A colorful screen lights up as Milo the Map appears. Roads, parks, and houses pop into place.
Maps show where places are. They help people see where they want to go before moving.
Milo can give directions. Words like left, right, near, and far help guide the way.
GPS helps Milo know where you are. GPS stands for Global Positioning System.
High above Earth, satellites send signals. Devices listen to these signals to find location.
Phones and cars use GPS. They match signals to maps to show where they are.
Milo updates routes when roads change. New paths help people avoid traffic and delays.
Maps do not drive cars. People stay in charge and make safe choices.
Learning directions builds confidence. Knowing where you are helps you feel calm.
When the trip ends, Milo rests. Tomorrow, new paths and places will appear again.
